title: ATRIUM controlled-label registry (JSON-LD)
description: Validator for the JSON-LD rendering of atrium_vocab.py -- the output of `python3 atrium_vocab.py --jsonld`. It is a STRUCTURAL gate, not a SKOS reasoner: it proves the document is well-formed JSON-LD with the node shapes this registry emits, that every concept carries a scheme and a prefLabel, and that only the four SKOS mapping properties ATRIUM has decided to use appear. Semantic integrity (mapping targets resolve, collection members are concepts, originator sets stay disjoint) is checked by `atrium_vocab.py --selftest`, which is the authority and runs in CI via para-drift.reusable.yml. Keep the two in step: this file describes the SHAPE, the selftest describes the MEANING.

@context.description: Prefix map. `atrium` is the one swappable base URI (atrium_vocab.SKOS_BASE); every ATRIUM-authored node id is rooted in it. The external prefixes are referenced, never minted here.

registry_version.description: atrium_vocab.REGISTRY_VERSION. Bumped when a concept is ADDED, REMOVED or RENAMED -- label-set membership is a contract other repos read. Editing a definition, note or mapping is additive and does not bump.

langString.description: An RDF language-tagged literal in JSON-LD expanded form.

node.description: Any node in the graph. A node is either typed (Concept / ConceptScheme / Collection) or is a bare mapping subject -- an external concept, such as a TEATER branch, that ATRIUM asserts a mapping FROM without redescribing it. Redescribing someone else's concept is exactly what this registry refuses to do, so an untyped mapping-only node is correct and expected.

allOf.description: A Concept must say which scheme it is in and carry a prefLabel. A concept with neither is unusable by any consumer and is almost always a table edited in one place and not the other.

A ConceptScheme must be titled and described, and must name the code that is authoritative for it -- carried as rdfs:comment 'authority: <path>'. Without that pointer the registry becomes a second source of truth rather than a view onto the first.
A Collection groups without asserting hierarchy, so it needs a label and at least one member.
An untyped node exists only to hang a mapping off an external concept, so it must carry at least one mapping property.
